points.title: Database design
points.must: The design-stage plan of the tables, fields, relationships and the type, size, key and validation of every field; its products are the ERD and the data dictionary.

points.title: Entity and attribute
points.must: Entity = a thing / person / event about which data is stored (becomes a table); attribute = one property of an entity (becomes a field), each with an example.

points.title: Primary and foreign key
points.must: PK uniquely identifies each record; FK is the PK of another table, used to link the tables — with an example (StudentID).

points.title: The steps of database design
points.must: Requirements → entities and attributes → relationships → ERD (resolve M:M) → data dictionary → CREATE TABLE.

points.title: ERD vs data dictionary
points.must: ERD = diagram of tables and relationships (overview); data dictionary = description of every field (detail for programmers).

points.title: Why design first
points.must: At least two reasons: errors found on paper; client can check reports; tables fit together; documentation for maintenance.

points.title: Finding entities
points.must: Underline the nouns; nouns with their own data and many instances are entities, single values are attributes; worked example (music school or own).

points.title: Choosing a primary key
points.must: Unique, never empty, does not change, short; create an ID field if no natural key; not a name or phone.

points.title: Degrees of relationship
points.must: 1:1, 1:M and M:M, each with an example and how it is implemented (FK on the many side; M:M needs a link entity).

points.title: Deciding the degree
points.must: Ask the question in both directions (one A has many B? one B has many A?) — with an example.

points.title: Drawing the ERD
points.must: Crow's foot notation sketch: boxes, PK/FK, single bar on the one side, crow's foot on the many side, labelled lines.

points.title: Resolving M:M
points.must: Why M:M cannot be stored (a field holds one value) and how a link entity with two FKs gives two 1:M relationships — e.g. Member–Book via Loan.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: At least two: M:M left in the ERD; FK on the one side; crow's foot at the wrong end; a single value made an entity; name as PK.
